ns2:section.sectionText: **** Find Information about restrictions and overrides: http://go.economics.illinois.edu/CoursesUndergrad **** Social Welfare, Income Inequality, and the Role of Government: This course presents certain economic perspectives on concepts of distributive justice, inequality and social welfare; it also studies attempts at quantifying them. It goes on to examine, in light of the said objectives and the various resource and informational constraints the economy faces, the government’s role in designing redistributive tax and expenditure policies. In the process, it discusses economic consequences of these policies highlighting the tradeoff between the society’s equity concerns and economic efficiency. Prerequisites: Econ 302 (Intermediate micro) Math 231 (calculus II) or a more advanced course in calculus.
